extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and reviewers submitting or handling manuscripts for PLOS One
extracted.subtask_description: Journal guidance describing PLOS One's editorial and peer review process, including initial checks, reviewer selection, decision types, revision and acceptance procedures, appeals, transfers, and peer review history publication options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision based on scientific rigor regardless of novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors make decisions on submissions based on scientific rigor, regardless of novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS One considers original research from across disciplines and assesses submissions by their scientific soundness rather than the perceived importance or novelty of the findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely responses and compliance with conduct policies
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors, editors, and reviewers are expected to reply to journal queries in a timely manner, and to comply with PLOS’ Code of Conduct for Editorial Board Members and policies on Ethical Peer Review and Standards for Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any concerns about correspondence or reviews should be raised to journal staff via plosone@plos.org.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial check — competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial quality checks identify potential issues such as competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts may be returned to authors for changes or clarifications at this stage if competing interest declarations are missing or problematic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial check — compliance with editorial policies and ethical standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial quality checks include assessing compliance with editorial policies and ethical standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions not meeting policy/ethical requirements may be returned for clarification or corrective action before editorial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial check — financial disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial quality checks include verification of required financial disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must disclose funding and financial relationships; missing or inadequate disclosures can trigger return or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial check — data availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial quality checks include assessing data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS One expects compliance with its data availability policies; lack of required data statements or access may require author action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial check — technical submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal performs an initial editorial assessment and screening for technical requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical/formatting issues found at submission may lead to the manuscript being returned to authors for correction prior to further editorial handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to an Academic Editor with relevant expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Each new submission is assigned to an Academic Editor with relevant expertise who reviews the manuscript against publication criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The handling Academic Editor is usually a member of the PLOS One Editorial Board, though occasionally a Guest Editor may be invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor assesses whether external peer review is needed
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor reviews the manuscript against publication criteria and determines whether reviews from additional experts are needed to evaluate the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This initial editorial review can result in rejection or progression to peer review depending on whether the manuscript meets the journal's criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The handling editor selects reviewers based on expertise, publication history, and past reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may indicate individuals who should not review their manuscript; such requests will be respected unless they interfere with objective assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer invitation and expected turnaround
rubrics_metrics.description: After agreeing to review, external peer reviewers typically have 10 days to submit their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal office will follow up with late reviewers and inform authors of delays if they occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-anonymized peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One uses single-anonymized peer review: reviewers remain anonymous unless they choose to sign their name to their review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers can choose to identify themselves by signing their review in the submission system; otherwise reviewer identities are not disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision-making process
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor considers reviewer feedback and their own evaluation of the manuscript in order to reach a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are communicated to the corresponding author with reviewer feedback and any other requirements from the journal office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available decision types
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision types available to editors are: Reject; Major revision; Minor revision; Accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On rare occasions, manuscripts may be withdrawn if a suitable Academic Editor or reviewers cannot be secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision resubmission timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors invited to revise will have 45 days to resubmit the revised manuscript for both a major or a minor revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 45-day period applies to both major and minor revisions unless otherwise communicated by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of revised manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, the revised manuscript is re-assigned to the original Academic Editor who may make a new decision or request additional input from external peer reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor will assess both the revised manuscript and the authors' response to reviewer comments when making a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-level acceptance (editorial accept then formal accept)
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One uses two levels of accept decision: an editorial accept (provisional, pending final checks) and a formal accept after final formatting/technical requirements are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once final requirements are fulfilled, the journal office will send a formal accept decision and the manuscript will move on to production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review history publication opt-in
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are offered the opportunity to publish the peer review history of their manuscript alongside the final article (and in some cases alongside a corresponding preprint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The peer review history package includes complete editorial decision letters for each revision, reviews, authors' responses including attachments, and reviewer names if reviewers signed their reviews. Authors are invited to opt-in via a form in the submission system if the manuscript is accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on publishing peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal reserves the right not to publish peer review history in special cases, for example, due to an ethical consideration such as the inclusion of information about a vulnerable population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors will withhold peer review history when publication would pose ethical risks or reveal sensitive information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of submissions to other journals requires author consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors can request that submissions (with reviewer reports, if relevant) rejected from one PLOS journal be transferred to another PLOS journal for further consideration; manuscripts will never be transferred between journals without an author’s consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS One may transmit reviews to other NPRC journals at the request of the authors; reviewers will be contacted for permission to transmit their names and reports are otherwise transmitted anonymously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation in Neuroscience Peer Review Consortium sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS One has partnered with the Neuroscience Peer Review Consortium to allow transmission of reviewer reports to other NPRC journals at the authors' request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will contact individual reviewers for permission to transmit their names to the recipient journal; reports can be used anonymously otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal requests must be made in writing to plosone@plos.org with the word 'Appeal PLOS One' in the subject line, and must include a completed Appeal Request Form; appeals by telephone or informal means are not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeal requests should not be sent to the Editor(s)-in-Chief of the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable grounds for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals will only be considered if (1) a reviewer or editor is thought to have made a significant factual error, or (2) a reviewer or editor’s objectivity may be compromised due to a documented competing interest, and (3) a reversal based on either of these grounds would change the original decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All appeal requests will be considered by at least one Staff Editor or Editorial Board member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances allowing PLOS to decline an appeal without review
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS may decline an appeal without review if integrity concerns contribute to a rejection decision, the decision is connected to an issue involving multiple submissions or articles, or PLOS determines that an appeal will be unable to satisfactorily resolve all issues underlying the editorial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declining without review is at PLOS's sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of manuscript during appeal and finality of appeal decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: While under appeal, a manuscript remains under formal consideration at PLOS One and should not be submitted elsewhere; decisions on appeals are final without exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should wait for the appeal outcome before pursuing submission to other journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors may withdraw manuscript if unable to secure suitable editor or reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: On rare occasions, if PLOS has been unable to secure a suitable Academic Editor or reviewers, we may withdraw the manuscript from the journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors will be informed of such withdrawals in a formal letter.
